issues.description: coerceNumber silently substitutes 0 for null/undefined, changing observable behavior from the original toNumber path.
issues.detail: The original panLinear/zoomLinear passed toNumber directly as lift, so null/non-numeric domain entries propagated as NaN. The new `coerceNumber = x => toNumber(x) ?? 0` substitutes 0 instead, producing plausible-but-wrong domain transforms. This contradicts the PR's claim of identical runtime behavior.

issues.description: panLog/zoomLog read domain[0] before the empty-domain guard, defeating the new check.
issues.detail: panLog and zoomLog compute `Math.sign(domain[0])` before invoking pan/zoom, so for empty domains Math.sign(undefined)=NaN runs first and log helpers are built on NaN before isNonEmpty throws. The guard should move into the public functions or before sign computation.

issues.description: New empty-domain throw is an undocumented breaking change for downstream callers.
issues.detail: Previously panLinear([], 0.5) returned [NaN, NaN] silently; now it throws. Downstream consumers in vega-scale or user code relying on NaN propagation will crash on upgrade. This warrants a changelog entry and likely a minor version bump rather than being labeled an internal refactor.

issues.description: Domain return type [number, number] overstates validity since lift/ground can yield NaN or Infinity.
issues.detail: log(sign) on sign-mismatched values and pow with fractional exponents on negatives produce NaN/Infinity, yet Domain is typed as a clean numeric tuple. The type is technically correct but misleads consumers expecting finite numbers. Document the possibility or widen/narrow accordingly.

issues.description: Empty-domain throw is only tested for panLinear and zoomLinear; six other entry points are uncovered.
issues.detail: panLog, panPow, panSymlog, zoomLog, zoomPow, zoomSymlog share the new precondition but have no empty-domain tests. Parameterized cases would enforce uniform contract behavior and would have caught the Math.sign-before-guard bug in the Log variants.

issues.description: peek non-empty overload may not narrow as intended for arrays typed as number[] after isNonEmpty.
issues.detail: Inside pan/zoom, `domain` remains typed as `number[]` even after the isNonEmpty guard returns true, so peek(domain) resolves to the `T | undefined` overload and d1 flows into arithmetic without true narrowing. Pass the narrowed reference, annotate the parameter as NonEmptyArray, or add a cast.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this TypeScript port quietly introduces two behavioral regressions despite being framed as a no-op refactor. coerceNumber maps null/undefined to 0 where the original toNumber propagated NaN, and panLog/zoomLog read domain[0] for Math.sign before the new isNonEmpty guard fires, so empty inputs never reach the intended throw. The new empty-domain runtime error is itself a breaking change that deserves a changelog entry and version bump. Test coverage for the new error path is limited to the Linear variants, and the Domain tuple type and peek overload narrowing are tighter than the runtime actually guarantees.
